observations:
Torah LM2 #22 is a short, concentrated halakhic-spiritual ruling — four sentences — about the nature of true humility (הַכְנָעָה). The key concepts present in the text are: הַכְנָעָה (humility), מֹחִין דְּקַטְנוּת (small-mindedness), מֹחִין דְּגַדְלוּת (large-mindedness), דַּעַת (wisdom/knowledge/consciousness), עֲנָוָה (being humble, the virtue), חֲנֻפָּה (flattery), and the figures of מֹשֶׁה (Moses) and יִרְמְיָה (Jeremiah).

For a new package to be proposed, the spec requires: 3+ concepts connected by explicit bechina language forming an independent domain not covered by existing packages.

None of the conceptual connections in this Torah are formed using explicit bechina language ('X הוא בְּחִינַת Y' or equivalent). The relationships are:
- מֹחִין דְּקַטְנוּת ↔ מֹחִין דְּגַדְלוּת: a polarity opposition, not a bechina equation
- הַכְנָעָה → דַּעַת: a prerequisite (eitza) — humility of the right kind requires knowledge
- הַכְנָעָה שֶׁאֵינוֹ כָּרָאוּי = חֲנֻפָּה: a Talmudic label applied by the Rabbis, not a Rebbe Nachman bechina formulation
- מֹשֶׁה = עָנָו מִכֹּל הָאָדָם: a biblical quotation (Numbers 12:3) establishing Moses as the archetype of true humility, not a bechina equation

The teaching's structure is analytical-argumentative throughout: it identifies a common error, explains why the error arises (entering מֹחִין דְּקַטְנוּת), provides the corrective principle (דַּעַת is required), cites the exemplar (Moses), and illustrates the failure mode via the Jeremiah–Hananiah episode. This entire structure is causal and definitional, not a web of bechina-connected concept-pairs.

The minimum threshold of 3 bechina-language connections is not met. NO_NEW_PACKAGES.
